title: autosynth: translator to synthesize tenant econ profiles + dry-run vet CLI
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add autosynth translator that converts tenant budget signals into candidate batching/caching/quantization profiles; new CLI 'redwood econ-vet' for dry-run validation; unit-econ telemetry and safety gates.
description:
Context and motivation: Several customers asked for a way to propose and validate tenant-level cost-saving defaults without applying them directly to runtime. This PR introduces an 'autosynth' translator that consumes tenant signals (budget hints, traffic patterns, SLA tiers) and synthesizes candidate prefill/batching, cache and quantization profiles. The main goal is to reduce manual profile curation and enable safe dry-runs before committing defaults to tenant configs.

What this PR does (high-level):
- Adds a translator service (pkg/economy/translator.go + runtime heuristics) that maps tenant signals to ranked candidate profiles (batch shapes, cache_windows, quant_presets) using a small rule graph and fallback heuristics.
- Introduces a CLI command 'redwood econ-vet' (src/cli/econ_vet.py) to perform deterministic dry-runs: it fetches tenant telemetry, synthesizes candidates, runs a lightweight simulator, and emits unit-economics delta estimates and a vetting verdict.
- Emits new telemetry streams (telemetry/unit_econ/*) to track estimated per-token cost, expected P50/P95 latency impact, and a risk_score used by rollouts.
- Adds safety gates: quantization loss budget, latency SLO guard, and an automatic rollback path for applied profiles.
- Adds API to export candidate suggestions as YAML for manual review and to store suggestions in the tenant suggestions bucket (configs/suggestions/*).

Why this is different from previous work: Existing autotuners propose defaults but often apply them directly or require heavy simulation infra. Autosynth focuses on an explicit translation layer + a low-friction vet CLI to let platform engineers and tenant owners preview results and opt in. It also aggregates unit economics delta in a compact, explainable format.

Checklist (PR-level):
- [x] Translator core: initial rule graph and translator implementation.
- [x] CLI: econ-vet with dry-run flag and YAML exporter.
- [x] Telemetry: unit_econ metrics added and wired to exporter.
- [x] Safety gates: quant/latency checks + rollback hooks.
- [x] Tests: unit tests for translator heuristics, end-to-end integration tests for CLI simulator.
- [x] Docs: short README for CLI and a usage snippet in docs/econ/README.md.

Commits (summary):
- f1f2e3a: initial translator skeleton and rule graph DSL (pkg/economy/translator.go, pkg/economy/rules_test.go)
- 9b8c7d6: add lightweight simulator library and cost delta estimator (pkg/sim/sim.go, tests)
- a3b4c5d: implement econ-vet CLI and YAML exporter (src/cli/econ_vet.py, configs/templates/econ_suggestion.yaml)
- c4d5e6f: wire telemetry and create unit_econ metrics (telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml)
- d7e8f9a: safety gates, rollback hooks and feature flag gating (runtime/safety_gate.go, configs/flags.yaml)
- e0f1d2b: docs, changelog and integration tests (docs/econ/README.md, test/integration/econ_vet_test.sh)

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/economy/translator.go (new) -- translation rules, ranking logic
- src/cli/econ_vet.py (new) -- user-facing CLI for dry-run vetting and export
- pkg/sim/sim.go (new) -- lightweight simulator used by vet to estimate deltas
- runtime/safety_gate.go (modified) -- safety checks and rollback path
- telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml (modified/added) -- new unit_econ metrics
- configs/templates/econ_suggestion.yaml (new) -- export template for suggestions
- docs/econ/README.md (new) -- usage and examples

Summary of implementation decisions:
- Keep the translator stateless and deterministic given the same telemetry snapshot so CLI results are reproducible.
- Use conservative defaults for quantization suggestions (prefer bfloat16/int8 mixed paths) and expose a loss_budget parameter for tenants with strict quality requirements.
- Simulator runs a resource-light tokenized synthetic workload using tenant shape statistics (p50/p95 length, temperature distribution) to estimate cost and latency deltas; it purposefully avoids full model execution to remain fast and safe.
- The vet CLI supports a --force-apply flag but by default only produces a suggested YAML and a human-readable verdict.

Review conversation (excerpt):
- Diego Alvarez (reviewer): "Nice separation between translator and simulator. Two asks: 1) add an explicit percentile breakdown for token savings (p50/p95) in the telemetry export, and 2) make sure the default quant presets include a fallback to non-quantized model when risk_score > 0.3"
- Maya Chen (author): "Addressed: added p50/p95 slices into telemetry export and adjusted translator ranking to include a risk_score clamp that vetoes quantized presets; see commit d7e8f9a for safety_gate changes."
- Priya Kapoor (reviewer): "CLI UX looks good. Please add an example of the YAML suggestion in the docs and a short example command in the integration test."
- Maya Chen: "Added docs/econ/README.md with sample output and updated integration test to assert YAML schema."
- Ethan Walker (approver): "Ran the CLI against a small tenant snapshot and confirmed simulated deltas are plausible. Approving pending CI pass."

CI and verification:
- Initial CI run failed one flaky telemetry unit test (pkg/telemetry/exporter_test.go) on the first attempt; root cause was a race in the test harness. The test was made deterministic and re-run.
- Final CI status: all checks pass (build, unit tests, integration/econ_vet_test, lint). See CI logs in the description for the passing run.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind experimental flag 'autosynth.v1' in configs/flags.yaml. No tenant defaults are changed by merging this PR.
- Post-merge rollout: enable flag in staging and run 'redwood econ-vet --tenant=<sample-tenants> --export' to generate suggestions and collect feedback. If suggestions are validated, a separate PR will propose automatic apply flows with additional guardrails.

Security and privacy considerations:
- Translator only consumes aggregated tenant telemetry (no raw user data) and exporters redact any tenant identifiers in the YAML output by default.
- Exported YAML is marked 'sensitive' when the tenant opted into telemetry redaction, and the CLI refuses to write to world-readable locations unless --insecure is passed with an explicit warning.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main on 2026-03-01 after approvals from Priya and Ethan and green CI.

Follow-ups tracked in Linear: ENG-9881 (auto-apply orchestration), ENG-9899 (audit logs for suggestion application), PM-447 (UX for tenant owners).
